name: Canada (federal)
standard: CAN/ASC-EN 301 549:2024 (identical to EN 301 549:2021 V3.2.1, WCAG 2.1 AA). Until the new regulations apply, federal departments must keep their existing WCAG 2.0 AA conformance.

laws.summary: Federally regulated entities must identify, remove and prevent barriers, including in ICT.

laws.cite: Regulations Amending the Accessible Canada Regulations (SOR/2025-255), Canada Gazette Part II, 2025-12-17
laws.summary: Adds digital accessibility duties requiring new or updated web pages, apps and documents to conform to CAN/ASC-EN 301 549:2024 to the extent feasible.

policy_docs.title: CIO direction on ICT accessibility; towards regulatory implementation
Summary of the changes to the Accessible Canada Regulations about digital accessibility

applies_to: Federal public sector; federally regulated private sector with 100+ employees (large 500+, medium 100–499). Excludes businesses with 99 or fewer employees and First Nations band councils (until December 2033).

deadlines.what: CAN/ASC-EN 301 549:2024 adopted by Accessibility Standards Canada
Digital amendments to the Accessible Canada Regulations published
TBS Standard on Web Accessibility and Guideline on Making IT Usable by All rescinded
Federal public sector: new or updated web pages and accessibility statements
Large and medium federally regulated businesses: web, mobile apps, digital documents, statements; federal public sector adds mobile apps and documents

requires: Newly created or updated digital content conforms to CAN/ASC-EN 301 549:2024
Departments: no regression on existing WCAG 2.0 AA conformance, plus alignment plans; Treasury Board submissions must meet or schedule compliance
mobile: explicit — the amended regulations name mobile applications (public sector from 2028-12-05).
procurement: The CIO direction points to procurement guides, and the rescinded guideline had strongly encouraged using CAN/ASC-EN 301 549 when acquiring IT.
enforcement: Administrative monetary penalties under the Accessible Canada Act; the ESDC summary cites amounts from $250 to $75,000 for violations. Enforcement is by the Accessibility Commissioner (not named in the pages opened).
notes: Correction to the brief: the Standard on Web Accessibility is no longer in force (rescinded 2026-03-02). The SOR number '2025-255' is inferred from the Gazette URL, which was not opened. The ACA URL is the standard Justice Laws path and was not opened. AMP maximums under the ACA itself are higher than the ESDC summary figure; verify before quoting.
